channel.title: Nomad Echo Sounds
channel.description: Real field recordings from the Tian Shan, Kazakhstan, measured for sleep and tinnitus masking. No AI audio.

item.title: How steady are nature sounds? Our measurement data
item.description: Open measurement data for real field recordings: loudness variation, sudden peaks, tone drift and low rumble for a mountain brook, a river and dawn birdsong.

item.title: Mountain River: recording notes and measurements
item.description: A loud but constant Tian Shan river, measured over 20 minutes: 0.62 dB loudness variation, no peaks above 10 dB, 0.6 dB drift, and the preparation chain.

item.title: Mountain Brook: recording notes and measurements
item.description: Our steadiest Tian Shan brook, measured: 0.31 dB loudness variation, no sudden peaks, one 3.5 dB channel imbalance we fixed, and the full preparation chain.

item.title: Which natural sounds mask tinnitus best?
item.description: We measured real mountain water recordings for loudness variation, sudden peaks and tone drift. Which natural sounds suit tinnitus masking, and which don't.

item.title: Is birdsong good for sleep? What the measurements show
item.description: A dawn chorus measured against a mountain brook: 42 loud events per minute and 12 times the loudness swing. Why birdsong works poorly for sleep.

item.title: Tian Shan field recordings: mountain water from the Ile Alatau
item.description: Where our mountain water sounds come from: spring 2026 field recordings at about 1,500 m in the Ile Alatau above Almaty, Kazakhstan, on a Zoom H5.
